title: Cold rebuild: Which services start?
summary: Rebuild Which services start? from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Which services start?** in *Environment, volumes and profiles*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: `.env` contains `API_KEY=abc`. The compose file never mentions `API_KEY`. Does the api container see `API_KEY`?
options: No: `.env` only feeds `${...}` interpolation in the compose file
Yes: every container gets all variables from `.env`
steps.explain: To pass it in, write `environment: API_KEY: ${API_KEY}`, or put it in a file referenced by `env_file:`.

steps.title: Rebuild Which services start? cold
prompt: Write `List<string> Active(Dictionary<string, List<string>> profiles, List<string> enabled, List<string> named)`.
- `profiles[s]` lists service s's profiles (empty when it has none).

- `named` are services named on the command line (`docker compose up adminer`). When any are named, Compose starts **only those**, whatever their profiles (it would add their `depends_on` too; leave that out here).
With nothing named, the services without profiles start, plus those with at least one enabled profile. Return the services that start, sorted alphabetically (ordinal).
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
List<string> Active(Dictionary<string, List<string>> profiles, List<string> enabled, List<string> named)
